Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 32, verse 1:

(p-222) Surat Alif Lam Mim al-Sajda (Surah of Prostration)

Its purpose is to warn the disbelievers with this Book, which gives joy to the righteous with entry into Paradise and salvation from the Fire. Its name "al-Sajda" (The Prostration) fits this purpose, by what its verse calls to of humility (ikhbat) and abandoning arrogance (istikbar). Likewise its name "Alif Lam Mim Tanzil," for it points to contemplation of the whole surah, and it is most clear regarding this purpose. "In the Name of Allah" (bismillah), the Possessor of Majesty and Honour, the Mighty, the Forgiving, "the Most Gracious" (al-Rahman), in the generality of glad tidings and warning, "the Most Merciful" (al-Rahim), who has placed in the hearts of His beloved the longing for Him and humble submission before Him. ﴿Alif Lam Mim﴾. Some of the secrets of these letters have been mentioned in al-Baqara and elsewhere. Among what has not preceded is that they are an indication that Allah, who encompasses in His knowledge, power, and every affair, sent Jibril, peace be upon him, to Muhammad (ﷺ), the Opener and the Seal, with a Book that is miraculous, indicating by its inimitability the truth of his prophethood, the oneness of the One who sent him, His justice toward the disobedient, and His favour toward the obedient. Glorified is He, Who set these letters at the beginnings of four of these surahs, so they exceeded the Ta-Sin surahs by one, and that is by the amount of the number by which it is emphasized. The beginning of counting with an increase is an indication that repetition was not intended merely for emphasis, but for the continuance of repetition, (p-223) indicating that these meanings fulfil the utmost firmness with no cessation for them. And Allah is the Guide.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 32, verse 2:

Since the aim of the surah before it (Surat Luqman) was to establish the wisdom of the One who sent down this Book, which is "an explanation of everything" (bayan kulli shay'), a quality that entails complete knowledge and perfect awareness, and since the surah was concluded after He (glorified is He) informed that He alone has knowledge of the keys of the unseen (al-mafatih), after warning of the matter of the Hour, it is established by this and by what came before it that He has affirmed nothing that others among the People of the Book or others could negate, and has negated nothing that others could affirm, nor affirmed any part of it. The result of this is that nothing among things, minute or grand, occurs without His knowing it, glorified and exalted is He. The most magnificent of these is the sending down of this Wise Reminder (al-dhikr al-hakim), which contains the affirmation of these sciences, together with the testimony of the inability to match it, and that it is from Allah. Therefore He said: ﴿The revelation of the Book﴾, that is, the one that gathers every guidance, as you see it being revealed gradually from the heaven. ﴿There is no doubt in it﴾, that is, its being from the heaven is beyond doubt, because the one who negates doubt and removes it, which is the miraculous nature (i'jaz) that accompanies it, is never separated from it. So whatever they say that contradicts this is obstinacy or ignorance, not doubt. It is ﴿from the Lord of the worlds﴾, that is, the Creator of them, the Manager of their interests. Therefore it is not permissible for reason, nor does it occur to the mind, nor does it fall into imagination, nor can it be conceived in the imagination, [that He would leave His creation, while He is the Wise Manager, without a Book that would be the cause of their sustenance], or that some part of His Book would reach this noble Prophet without His command. Thus it cannot be imagined that some part of it is not the speech of Allah, and then imagined that it is His speech, but that he took it from some of the People of the Book. For this is not done even with an angel, so how with the King of kings? And how with the One who knows the secret and the open, whose knowledge encompasses the hidden and the manifest? If anyone were to attribute to Him something He had not permitted, He would not have strengthened him with miracles.

When He confirmed this over those lengthy periods, especially the miraculous nature of everything attributed to Him through the miracles, and claimed by Him, and this is the ultimate of what is in Al 'Imran, just as the beginning of Luqman was the ultimate of the beginning of the unrestricted Qur'an. Imam Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: When Surat al-Rum comprised what has been pointed out of the admonition with the wonders which He (glorified and exalted is He) deposited in the world of the heavens and the earth, and of the mention of the fitrah (innate disposition), then it was followed by Surat Luqman, as a clarification that the totality of those signs is among the verses of the Book, its evidences and its proofs, and that He has guided whomever He wills to the path of the fitrah, even if He did not test him with what He tested many of those mentioned with. So it did not avail them, and they were called but did not respond, and the warnings were repeated upon them but they did not heed them. For all of that, of guidance and misguidance, occurs by His will and His preceding determination. And He (glorified is He) followed that with what alerts the one who reflects to its soundness, so He said: ﴿And whoever submits his face to Allah while he is a doer of good has grasped the most trustworthy handhold﴾ [Luqman: 22]. He informed that salvation and happiness lie in submission to Him and to what befalls of His decrees. He consoled His Prophet (ﷺ) and made him patient by saying: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, let not his disbelief grieve you﴾ [Luqman: 23]. Then He mentioned the refuge of all, compelled and returning, whose necessity He judges, since the matter is clear, to Him (exalted is He), so He said: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah"﴾ [Luqman: 25]. Then He admonished all by His saying: ﴿Your creation and your resurrection are not but as one soul﴾ [Luqman: 28], that is, that this is not difficult for Him (glorified is He) nor hard, and the few and the many are equal to Him. Then He alerted with what explains this, namely the entering of the night into the day and the day into the night, and the running of the ships by His grace: ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth﴾ [Luqman: 30]. Then He confirmed what preceded of their returning to Him in hardships, so He said: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shade, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Luqman: 32]. When He (glorified and exalted is He) delivers them and saves them, they return to their evil states. This is while they have witnessed His kindness toward them and His taking hold of their hands in times of hardship, and they have acknowledged that He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth and the Subjugator of the sun and the moon. That is a witness from their own condition, by their conformity to what He has decreed for them and their stopping at the limits of the preceding determinations. ﴿And whoever submits his face to Allah while he is a doer of good has grasped the most trustworthy handhold﴾ [Luqman: 22]. Then He (glorified is He) turned to all of them, called them to His piety, warned them of the Day of return and its severity, warned them against being deceived, and informed them that He alone has knowledge of the Hour, (p. 226) and of the sending down of rain, and of knowledge of what is in the wombs, and of what will be earned, and where every creature will die. So when Surat Luqman, by what it has made clear of its contents, comprised alerting and stirring toward what was mentioned, and made known His singularity (glorified is He) in the creation of all and their possession, He (exalted is He) followed it with what judges by recording the soundness of the Book, that it is from Him, and that what it contains of proofs and demonstrations removes every doubt and dispels every uncertainty. So He said: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim﴾ [Luqman: 1]. ﴿The revelation of the Book, there is no doubt in it, from the Lord of the worlds﴾. ﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"? Rather, it is the truth from your Lord﴾ [al-Sajdah: 3], that is, does this occur from them after its clarity and the manifestness of its evidences? Then He followed that by His saying: ﴿You have no protector or intercessor besides Him﴾ [al-Sajdah: 4], which completes His saying: ﴿And whoever submits his face to Allah﴾ [Luqman: 22], and His saying: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "Allah"﴾ [Luqman: 25], and His saying: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shade, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Luqman: 32], and His saying: ﴿Fear your Lord﴾ [Luqman: 33]. ﴿You have no protector or intercessor besides Him. Will you not then remember?﴾ [al-Sajdah: 4], by what has been reminded to you. Do you not see the matter of Luqman and his guidance through merely the proof of his fitrah? So what is wrong with you, after the reminder, the rebuke of warnings, the successive proofs and the consecutive signs, that you hesitate to travel toward your Lord, while you have acknowledged that He is your Creator, and you turn to Him when you are in need? Then He informed His Prophet (ﷺ) of the return of those who opposed, and of their response at a time when return will not benefit them and response will not avail them, so He said: ﴿If only you could see when the criminals will bow their heads before their Lord﴾ [al-Sajdah: 12]. (p. 227) Then He (glorified is He) informed that what occurs from them is only by His will and a preceding wisdom, so that the one granted success and certain would take himself to submission. So He said: ﴿And if We had willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾ [al-Sajdah: 13], as We did with Luqman, and whomever We willed to grant success. Then He mentioned their division according to the preceding determinations, so He said: ﴿Is one who is a believer like one who is defiantly disobedient? They are not equal﴾ [al-Sajdah: 18]. Then He mentioned the destination of the two groups and the end of the two parties. Then He followed that with the bad condition of those who were reminded and turned away, so He said: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the verses of his Lord and then turns away from them?﴾ [al-Sajdah: 22]. The discourse extended to the end of the surah. Ended.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 32, verse 3:

When this [matter], which he had presented at the beginning of the surah in this manner, became a clear proof and a decisive evidence that [this] Book is from Allah, it was, as al-Baghawi and al-Razi related in *al-Lawami'*, as if it were said: "Did they believe in it?" ﴿Or do they say﴾, despite that which no sensible person doubts, ﴿"He has invented it"﴾, that is, he deliberately fabricated its falsehood.

Since the answer was that they indeed say, "He has invented it," and its answer was that it is not invented, because of the inimitability (i'jaz) that accompanies it, there followed his saying: ﴿Rather, it is the truth﴾, that is, the established, whose stability is not matched by the stability of any of the Books before it, ﴿from your Lord﴾, the one who has been good to you by sending it down and making it firm. He addressed it to him specifically, indicating that no one else truly understands its reality as it should be understood. (p. 228)

When He, glory be to Him, explicitly mentioned His favour to him, ﷺ, He also indicated, by its cause, His favour through him to all the Arabs. So He said, singling out the warning because the context calls for it according to the closing of Luqman: ﴿so that you may warn a people﴾, that is, people possessing strength, vigour, protection and capability to carry out what they were commanded, ﴿to whom no warner had come﴾, that is, no messenger in these recent times. This is based on the saying of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the intended meaning is the fatrah (the interval between prophets). This is supported by the affirmation of the preposition in His saying ﴿before you﴾ [that is, in actuality], they witnessed him or their fathers witnessed him. As for in meaning and potential, the religion of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, was among them until 'Amr ibn Luhayy changed it. All of them knew that Ibrahim, peace and blessings be upon him, did not worship an idol nor divine by arrows, and this is as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿There is no nation but that a warner has passed among them﴾ (Fatir: 24), that is, his law and religion. The warner is not restricted to one who directly came; Abu Hayyan drew attention to this. It may be said: no one came to them to warn them specifically about what they altered of the religion of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. As for Isma'il, his son, peace be upon him, he was a bearer of good tidings and not a warner, because they did not oppose him. Better than all of that is what al-Baghawi transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, and Muqatil, that this refers to the fatrah which was between 'Isa and Muhammad ﷺ, for it is related that 'Isa, peace be upon him, when he sent his messengers to the horizons, sent a messenger to the Arabs. (p. 229)

When he mentioned the cause of the sending down, he followed it with the cause of the warning, and said: ﴿so that they may be guided﴾, that is, so that their condition in the customary course of affairs would be that of one whose guidance is hoped for to the perfection of the Law. As for monotheism, there is no excuse for anyone regarding it, given the proof of reason that Allah established, together with what the messengers, upon them be blessings and peace, from Adam onward, left in clear transmitted form through the traces of their calls and the remnants of their indications. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said to one who asked him about his father: "My father and your father are in the Fire," and he said: "Do not boast of your fathers who died in the Jahiliyyah; by Him in whose hand is my soul, the dung beetle rolling its dung is better than them." Other reports besides these decree that whoever died before his call upon polytheism, he is for the Fire.

When what was established in the previous verse was confirmed, namely that He, exalted is He, is characterized by perfect knowledge, and that this (the Qur'an) is from Him and by His knowledge without doubt, and since this is a matter that deserves concern and attention, because the aim [which] the affair of religion is built upon has been specified, and He concluded what He mentioned of His affair here by making their being guided stand in the place of hope through His warning (ﷺ), (p-230) He followed it with an explanation of that by bringing into existence the world of bodies and creation, then the world of spirits and command, and the encompassing of knowledge of all of that in a manner that leads their reflection to guidance. So He said, resuming and explaining a matter that includes its sending down, expressing Himself with the Greatest Name (al-ism al-a'zam), because creating and managing in the manner of exclusivity to Him requires it: ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the One who comprises all attributes of perfection, alone, ﴿who created the heavens﴾ all of them, ﴿and the earth﴾ in its entirety, ﴿and what is between them﴾ of the benefits, both tangible and immaterial.

Since this abode was built upon the wisdom of causes, as was indicated in Luqman, and since a thing made gradually is more perfectly done, He said: ﴿in six days﴾, as its detailed explanation will come in Fussilat. Although He was able to do that in less than the blink of an eye, [and in Fussilat will come the secret of the period being six.]

Since the management of these, their preservation, the care of their interests, and the undertaking of their affair was, after the affair of their bringing into existence, a matter of great magnitude, He indicated its greatness by the particle of delay [and the expression by the form of ifti'al (the eighth verbal form)], so He said: ﴿Then He istawa over the Throne﴾, that is, [an istiwa' the like of which they had not known, namely that] He undertook [its management and] the management of [what it contains] Himself, with no partner, no deputy in His place, and no vizier, as you are accustomed among the kings of this world when their domains expand, their borders grow distant, and their regions become remote. This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He, resuming as an answer to one who seems to have said: "The Throne is very far from us, so who has been appointed to act on His behalf in our affairs?" For this reason the speech [turned] to address (the second person), because it is more effective in alerting: ﴿You have not, besides Him﴾, because everything other than Him is beneath Him and under His dominion, ﴿any protector﴾, which indicates the generality of the negation: that is, one who takes charge of your affairs, looks after your interests, and gives you victory when something of what you are warned about befalls you, ﴿nor any intercessor﴾ who intercedes with Him concerning your management or concerning any one of you without His permission. [This is a metonymy for His nearness to everything, His encompassing of it, and that His encompassing of all His creation is on an equal footing, with no distance at all between Him and anything.]

Since they acknowledged that creation is His creation and command is His command, and knew that no governor comes to rule on behalf of any king except with a proof from him that he establishes upon [the people] of the town to which he was sent or in which he acts as deputy, and that no intercessor intercedes for them except that he has a means to Him, this rebuke against them is consequent upon it in His saying: ﴿Will you not then remember?﴾, that is, a great remembrance, by what the explicit wording points to, of what you know: that He is the Creator alone, and that there is no proof for any of what you have associated with Him by which it qualifies to be His (partner), and no means for any of them to Him by which it could qualify for intercession on your behalf, and none of them has informed you of anything [of that]. So how do you oppose, in these matters, which are the most important of the important, since their consequence is the ruin of the human being himself, let alone what is less than them, your intellects and what your habits have run upon? You rationalize in them what is impossible, you are content with "he said, she said," (p-231) and you gamble with your souls, children, and wealth on it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 32, verse 5 (part 1 of 2):

When He had negated that He has any partner or minister in creation, He mentioned how He acts in this great dominion which He originated in six days, from the world of spirits and command (amr). He said, beginning a new sentence and explaining what is meant by "istiwa'" (establishment or settling): ﴿He manages the affair﴾, that is, every affair of this world, by acting in it the way one who looks at the ends of things acts, in order to perfect their final outcomes and necessary consequences, just as He looked at their beginnings to firm up their initial stages and determinations. He does not entrust any part of it to any of His creatures. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': "This is evidence that His establishment on the Throne means the manifestation of power, and the Throne is the place where management is displayed, not the floor (qa'r) of what is managed."

Since the intended audience, the Arabs, were concerned only with the management of what they could witness of the world, He said, singling out (the sky): ﴿from the heaven﴾, meaning that this affair which He perfected descends, as one who looks at the ends of what he knows perfects it, ﴿to the earth﴾, without touching on what is above that. Moreover, "heaven" (sama') includes every high thing, so the entire world is included.

Since ascent is harder than descent according to customary habits, and was therefore regarded as remote, He indicated this with His words:

﴿Then it ascends﴾, that is, the affair (amr) rises, a single affair, and this is a fine use of the device of istikhdam (using one word in two senses), ﴿to Him﴾, that is, the dominion ascends to God, meaning to the place which He honored or commanded to be in, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed I am going to my Lord﴾ [al-Saffat 37:99], and ﴿Whoever leaves his home emigrating to God and His Messenger﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:100], and similar. Or (it ascends) to the place from which the descent of the management began, which is the heaven. It is as though it is ascending through ascending stairways (ma'arij), which are steps as you know them among yourselves, ﴿in a day﴾ of the days of this world, ﴿the measure of which is﴾, if the one ascending were one of you by your usual standards, ﴿a thousand years of what you count﴾ of your years which you know.

What indicates this estimate is something from customary usage and something from the wording. As for the wording, it is the expression "kana" (was/is), along with the fact that the sentence remains intact without it if something else were intended. As for customary usage, a wealthy person builds a great, lofty house in, say, a year. When he finishes it, his servant climbs to its top in less than two flights of sand-dune steps. The proportion of that climb to the time of building is then an insignificant fraction. And this concerns a created being in need, so what do you think of the One who created creation in six days, who is independent of everything and capable of everything?

The apparent sense of the expression is that this estimate of a thousand years is for the distance between heaven and earth, on the basis that the starting point and the endpoint are not included. If we wish to apply this verse to the verse of Sa'il (al-Ma'arij), we take this (distance) as relative to the ascent of one of us standing upright, if that were possible. The earth is counted as one, although its multiplicity is, as it has been said, reckoned by its climes (aqalim). To this is added the thickness of the heavens and what lies between them. To the total is added a quantity equal to half of it, for the distance of the curvature in building the stairs and the winding path, which is like the circumference of a circle relative to the chord that divides it into two halves so that we can ascend. This is the measure of half the distance of the straight line plus a small amount. For when you divide a circle by a chord, the arc between the two ends of the chord, as part of the circumference of the semicircle, equals the chord once and a half, plus a small amount that may be added for the windings of the stairs. When we do this, the distance between one surface of the Kursi, the convex (outer) surface, and the opposite surface, according to its penetration from both sides and the penetration of the seven heavens' layers, is thirty-two thousand years. This is because each heaven is allotted two thousand years. This is understood from this context: from the concave side of the heaven to the surface of the earth on which we stand is a journey of a thousand years, and the distance between each two heavens is like the distance between heaven and earth, and the thickness of each heaven is likewise. So the distance from one surface of the earth to the surface of the upper Kursi is sixteen thousand years, and the distance from the surface of the earth to the highest surface of the Kursi on the other side is likewise. Then to the total, which is thirty-two thousand years, is added the thickness of the earth, which is a thousand years, making thirty-three thousand years. To this is added what is for the windings, which is half that distance plus something, making seventeen thousand years. That makes fifty thousand years. I have made the upper surface of the Kursi the endpoint, because the custom is that no one ascends to the throne of a king except him, and that desires end short of it, and indeed no one ascends to his Kursi. This consideration will come later in the final aspect.

If we say that the earths are seven, placed one above the other as lofty spheres, not interpenetrating, and we include the Throne in the count, then we say: together with the Kursi and the heavens, they are nine. Their two sides enclosing the earth are eighteen layers. The earths are seven, so that is twenty-five layers. Each one, along with what lies between it and the next, according to the apparent sense of the verse, is two thousand years. This number is doubled, so it becomes fifty thousand. This aspect is the clearest of the aspects and the closest to the meaning of the verse, and it does not need any addition for the bending of the stairs. It is also permissible to say: the secret, and God knows best, in making what travels five hundred years, as in the hadith, a thousand years, is because of the winding path. The hadith is not an explicit text about a specific journey, so as to avoid interpreting it. Rather, it has come in different wordings: among them five hundred, and among them seventy-two years, and among them seventy-one, and others. So each wording must be applied to a specific mode of travel. We say: the five hundred is for one ascending on a straight staircase, like a palm-trunk ladder for example. The seventy-two is for the travel of a bird. The thousand, as in the verse, is for a winding staircase. This is indicated by what al-Tirmidhi narrated, and he said: its chain is good (hasan), from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, may God be pleased with both of them, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said:

"If a bullet like this one, and he pointed to something like a skull, were sent down from the heaven to the earth, and it is a journey of five hundred years, it would reach the earth before night. And if the chain were sent down, it would travel forty autumns, night and day, before it reached its root or its bottom." [Or one may say: the thousand is for the whole management by descent and ascent.]

And God knows best. If we consider the beginning to be included, then the thousand is from the surface of the earth on which we stand to the convex surface of the heaven, so that the verse agrees with the hadith which says that between the earth and the heaven is five hundred years, and the thickness of the heaven is likewise, and likewise the rest of the heavens and the Throne. We include the Throne in the count and say: the earths are seven, interpenetrating like the heavens, each one within the next. The one we are on is the highest of them and encompasses them all, so it is in the position of the Throne relative to the heavens. The seven heavens from both of its sides come to fourteen thousand, and the earths likewise, so that is twenty-eight thousand. The Throne and the Kursi from both of its sides come to four, so that is thirty-two thousand. To this is added what increases the curvature of the ascent-paths by which ascent is possible for us, which is half the distance of the whole plus something. The half is sixteen thousand. We make the something that has not been determined for us two thousand. That makes eighteen thousand. Added to the thirty-two thousand, the whole is fifty thousand. This could be the case with the heavens together with the earths, and the whole is congruent and interpenetrating. So that is twenty-eight layers from the upper surface of the seventh heaven to its upper surface on the other side, so that is twenty-eight thousand years, for each body five hundred. Since its distance from the other body is likewise, that is a thousand. He doubled it relative to descent and ascent, so it becomes fifty-six thousand. From it fifty thousand is counted, and the fraction is dropped. But this aspect contradicts the apparent sense of the verse in Sa'il, which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a day the measure of which is fifty thousand years﴾ [al-Ma'arij 70:4], because there is no mention of descent in it.

And God knows best.

Each of these aspects is more firmly grounded than what al-Baydawi said in the surah Sa'il, and closer to understanding and customary usage. If his apparent position was that he made the eighteen thousand from the highest canopies (suradiqat) of the Throne to the highest of its canopies on the other side, then there is no evidence for this, and no custom supports the climbing of servants to the highest canopy, which is the highest part of it. God knows best.

Ishaq ibn Rahawayh narrated from Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger (ﷺ) said:

"The distance between the lowest heaven and the earth is five hundred years, and the distance between each heaven and the one next to it is five hundred years, up to the seventh heaven. The earth is like that. And the distance between the seventh heaven and the Throne is like all of that."

Know that the view that the earths are seven is the apparent one, in accordance with the apparent sense of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿God is He who created seven heavens and of the earth their like﴾ [al-Talaq 65:12]. It is supported by what al-Shaykhan [al-Bukhari and Muslim] and others narrated from Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said:

"Whoever usurps the measure of a span of land, God will collar him with it from the seven earths." In a narration of al-Baghawi: "He will be sunk into the seven earths."

Ibn Hibban narrated in his Sahih from Abu Hurayra, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said:

"Indeed, when death attends the believer..." [he mentioned it until he said]: "As for the disbeliever, when his soul is seized, he is taken to the earth, and the guardians of the earth say: 'We have not found a smell more foul than this.' And so it is brought down to the lowest earth."

Al-Mundhiri said: it is in Ibn Majah with a sound chain.

What supports those who say that they are interpenetrating like spheres, with a space between each two earths like the heavens, is what al-Hakim narrated and graded as sound from Abdullah ibn Amr, may God be pleased with them both, who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said:

"Indeed the earths, between each earth and the one next to it, are a journey of five hundred years. The uppermost of them is on the back of a fish..." to the end of the hadith. It is at the end of al-Mundhiri's al-Targhib, at the end of the section on the horrors of the Resurrection, in its chains and shackles.

Abu 'Ubayd [al-Qasim] ibn Salam narrated in Gharib al-Hadith from Mujahid, may God have mercy on him, that he said: the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram) has its direction (muna) forbidden from the seven heavens and the seven earths, and that it is the fourth of fourteen houses: in every heaven there is a house, and in every earth there is a house. If they were to fall, some of them would fall upon others. Muna here means its intended direction and what is opposite it.

In Majma' al-Zawa'id of the hafiz Nur al-Din al-Haytami, it is mentioned that Imam Ahmad narrated through the route of al-Hakam ibn Abd al-Malik, who is weak, from Abu Hurayra, may God be pleased with him, who said:

"While we were with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), a cloud passed by. He said: 'Do you know what this is?' We said: 'God and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'It is the rain-cloud and the corners of the earth, which God drives to whoever does not thank Him and does not call upon Him. Do you know what is above you?' We said: 'God and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'The raqi' is a restrained wave and a protected ceiling. Do you know how far it is between you and it?' We said: 'God and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'Five hundred years' journey.' Then he said: 'Do you know what is above it?' We said: 'God and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'Another heaven. Do you know how far it is between you and it?' We said: 'God and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'Five hundred years' journey,' until he counted seven heavens. Then he said: 'Do you know what is above that?' We said: 'God and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'The Throne.' He said: 'Do you know how far it is between it and the seventh heaven?' We said: 'God and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'Five hundred years' journey.' Then he said: 'What is this beneath you?' We said: 'God and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'Earth.' He said: 'Do you know what is beneath it?' We said: 'God and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'Another earth. Do you know how far it is between them?' We said:"

Allah and His Messenger know best!
He said:
"A journey of seven hundred years, until he counted seventy earths. Then he said: 'By Allah, if you were to lower a rope, it would descend [to Allah].' Then he recited: ﴿He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is Knowing of all things﴾ [al-Hadid: 3]." He said:
Al-Tirmidhi narrated it, except that he mentioned that between each earth and the next earth there are five hundred years, whereas here it is seven hundred. And at its end he said: "If you were to lower a rope, it would descend upon Allah." Perhaps he meant: upon the Throne of Allah, or upon His judgment, His knowledge and His power, meaning that He is in His dominion and His grip, not outside anything of His affair. And Allah knows best. I saw in Jami' al-Usul by Ibn al-Athir, after his citation of this hadith, [the following text]: Abu 'Isa said: The Messenger of Allah's ﷺ recitation of the verse indicates that he meant: it would descend upon the knowledge of Allah, His power and His authority, and this would support the view that they are spheres that are congruent and interlocking, and Allah knows best. [This is] what was narrated: that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"The seven heavens and the seven earths, in the Throne, are nothing but like a ring thrown down in a desert." He did not say "like a dirham," for example, and so on. (p-242) What Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umar, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Ibn Hibban narrated from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, a long hadith in which the prophets are mentioned, and in it the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Do you know what the likeness of the heavens and the earth is in the Kursi?"
I said: "No, unless you teach me what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has taught you." He said: "The likeness of the heavens and the earth in the Kursi is like a ring thrown down in a desert, and the excellence of the Kursi over the heavens and the earth is like the excellence of the desert over that ring." Its origin is with al-Nasa'i, al-Tayalisi and Abu Ya'la. Likewise, what the author of al-Firdaws narrated from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet ﷺ said:
"The seven heavens, in the greatness of Allah, are nothing but like a hanging gourd." And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿His Kursi encompasses the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255] indicates that the Kursi encompasses everything from all sides. [And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If you are able to pass through the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass through﴾ [al-Rahman: 33] is explicit in that, for passing through (nufudh) is used for piercing, especially with the expression "min" rather than "fi." Likewise His saying concerning the sky: ﴿And it has no rifts﴾ [Qaf: 6].]
And Allah is the Granter of success.

Now that this has been established regarding the world of bodies and creation, and then the world of spirits and command, which shows the comprehensiveness of power, and since the one whose power is comprehensive must necessarily have all-encompassing knowledge, its result is inevitably: ﴿That﴾, i.e., the God of lofty station and manifest signs, ﴿is the Knower of the unseen﴾, whose keys were mentioned at the end of the preceding passages concerning spirits, command, and creation.

Since He gave precedence to knowledge of the unseen because it is higher, and since one who knows the unseen may not know the witnessed (because he does not see it), He said: ﴿and the witnessed﴾, from all of that, of which is the sending down of the Qur'an upon you and its arrival to you, ﴿the Mighty﴾, who overcomes everything and whom nothing overcomes. And since it might be that a captious person would find fault in His might on account of the neglect of the disobedient, He said: ﴿the Merciful﴾, [i.e.] who singled out from among His servants those who bear the obligation with mercy in sending down the Books through the tongues of the Messengers, and made clear to them what the Divinity is pleased with, after He had encompassed all creatures with the attribute of the Most Merciful (al-Rahmaniyyah) after bringing them into existence from non-existence, through kindness and bounty.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 32, verse 7:

When he had explicitly mentioned the attribute of Mercifulness (al-Rahimiyya), as the context required it, he alluded to the attribute of Compassionateness (al-Rahmaniyya) and said: ﴿Who made everything He created good﴾. Since this goodness is general, he specified it by describing it, according to the reading of al-Madani and al-Kufi, with His saying: ﴿He created it﴾. Thus he clarified that this is by perfection and firm ordering, as Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, explained it, in terms of shaping and forming, the splitting of the senses, the preparation of the faculties, and the bestowing of meanings (al-ma'ani), with variation in all of that. The substitution (al-ibdal) in the reading of the rest of the readers points to this. He expressed it with "good" because what is done in accordance with wisdom is good, even if the ignorant and deficient person sees it as ugly.

When animals were the noblest of the kinds, and the human being was the noblest of them, he specified him for mention so that the proof of Divine Oneness would be established in the self just as it had been established earlier in the horizons. So he said, indicating the resurrection: ﴿And He began the creation of man﴾, i.e., the one who is the primary intended addressee of this Qur'an, ﴿from clay﴾, i.e., from that which has no origin in life, by the creation of Adam, peace be upon him, from it.

Since the fashioning of clay into this frame, in this form and with these meanings, is a monumental matter, he indicated it with the distal particle in His saying: ﴿Then He made his offspring﴾, i.e., his progeny, which "yansull" (slips forth), i.e., comes out, ﴿from an extract﴾, i.e., from something drawn out (maslūl), meaning extracted from him, ﴿from a fluid, despicable﴾, i.e., base, weak and little, poured out and spilled. It is on the pattern fa'īl in the sense of maf'ūl. He indicated the greatness of what follows of His creation and development with His saying:

ثُمَّ سَوّاهُ — that is, He balanced him (عَدَلَهُ) for what is intended of him, through shaping (التَّخْطِيطِ), forming (والتَّصْوِيرِ) and originating meanings (وإبْداعِ المَعانِي). ﴿And breathed into him of His Spirit﴾. The rūḥ (spirit) is that by which the living is distinguished from the dead (المَيِّتِ) (p-245). The idāfa (genitive construction, "of His") is one of honour (لِلتَّشْرِيفِ). How great a dignity, how exalted it is, that it is attributed to Allah!

When the listeners had given their ears to this discourse, and they were deserving that the speaker should increase their attentiveness and benefit, he turned the address toward them, saying: ﴿And He made for you﴾, that is, through the causes He set in the body, ﴿hearing﴾ [that is], by which you perceive the sounding meanings (المَعانِيَ المُصَوِّتَةَ), and He used the singular for it because of the slight variation in it when it is sound. ﴿And sight﴾, by which you perceive meanings and visible bodies (الأعْيانَ القابِلَةَ). [Perhaps He placed sight first because one benefits from both at the time of birth, and He placed hearing before it because at that time it is firmer than sight; for this reason midwives bind the eye lest light weaken it. As for the intellect, it is acquired only gradually, so He delayed its place and said:] ﴿and hearts﴾, that is, the hot, glowing, turning lumps (المُضَغُ الحارَّةُ المُتَوَقِّدَةُ المُتَحَرِّفَةُ), namely the hearts deposited with the natural dispositions of intellects, which differ among them to an extreme degree. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': He made him (that is, man) composed of a spiritual and a corporeal element, and of a higher and a lower element; He gathered in him both worlds through his soul and his body, and combined the two realms through his intellect and his senses, and he was elevated above both levels through the connection of the Supreme Command to him by verbal revelation, and he surrendered the matter to the One to whom belong creation and command, a surrender that is chosen and voluntary (p-246). And [since] they did not hasten to faith when reminded of these great blessings, He said: ﴿Little is it that you give thanks﴾, that is, and much is it that you disbelieve.

When they said, "Muhammad is not a messenger, God is not one, and the resurrection is not possible," He pointed to the validity of the message by negating doubt about the Book. Then He pointed to God's oneness through the comprehensiveness of His power and the all-encompassing reach of His knowledge in originating creation in a manner that is a blessing for them. He concluded by expressing wonder at their disbelief. Their dismissal of the resurrection, which is the third principle, was among the greatest of their disbeliefs. He spoke, expressing wonder at their denial of it after the wonder expressed in His words, ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ [al-Sajdah: 3], turning away from addressing them to signal anger at their words, ﴿And they said﴾, denying what He had established in the original natural disposition (fitrah) and what the messengers had alerted to, so that no rational person who has encountered any part of wisdom could dislike it: ﴿"When we have become lost﴾ [idhā], meaning, "Shall we be resurrected when we have become lost," i.e., gone, perished, and vanished ﴿in the earth﴾ by becoming dust like its dust, such that no part of it is distinguished from another. Abu Hayyan, following al-Baghawi, al-Zamakhshari, Ibn Jarir al-Tabari, and others, said: the origin of this is from "ḍalla al-mā' fī al-laban," meaning when water is lost in milk, i.e., it disappears. Then they repeated the denying interrogative (al-istifhām al-inkārī) to increase the sense of improbability, saying: ﴿"Shall we indeed be in a new creation?"﴾ — one that encompasses us while we are contained within it.

Since their statement includes a denial of God's power, and since they acknowledged what necessarily follows from it, namely the affirmation of power to resurrect, through creating creation, delivering from every distress, and similar things, He indicated this with His words: ﴿Rather﴾, meaning they are not deniers of His power, glory be to Him. Rather, ﴿they are in meeting with their Lord﴾, the One who does good by originating and sustaining, subjecting to them everything that benefits them in the Hereafter, for reckoning, as living, upright beings, just as they were in the world. The indication through this attribute is that it is not fitting for the Good One to spoil His goodness by abandoning retribution against the wrongdoer who exists on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Disbelievers﴾, meaning deniers of the resurrection out of obstinacy, concealing what is in their natures of its proofs, because of the desire that overpowered them, which leads them to actions from which pride in accepting the truth and aversion to affirming what necessarily entails deficiency of intellect prevented them from turning back.

When he had mentioned their disbelief in resurrection and followed it with their stubbornness, and their denial rested on the mixing of the body's parts with the dust after they had turned into dust, so that in their view it was impossible to separate them from the rest of the dust, He showed that this is easy for Him by reminding them of things they acknowledge, which are similar to it and even more subtle. He then said, resuming: ﴿Say﴾, that is (p-٢٤٨) as an answer to them concerning their doubt: ﴿The angel of death who has been entrusted with you will take your souls﴾, that is, he will seize your spirits completely from your bodies, after they had been mixed with all the parts of the body, with no distinction between one and the other in any way you know, by any kind of stratagem. Then He indicated that his action is by His power, and that this is extremely easy for Him, by using the passive form of the verb, so He said: ﴿who has been entrusted with you﴾, that is, the Creator has commissioned him for this purpose. He is one of His servants, and he does what he is commanded. Then the body lies there with no spirit in any part of it, yet it remains in its state, complete, with no deficiency in any part of it that would give cause for claiming a defect. If this is the act of one of His servants, whom He has empowered for it, and who carries it out as you see, then how can anything be deemed far-fetched for the Lord of the worlds and the Manager of all creation? The fact that the mixing of the spirit with the body is stronger than the mixing of the body's dust with the rest of the dust, since some skilled people may sometimes identify some of this by a kind of evidence such as smell or the like, makes this even clearer.

When this decisive proof, which is manifest and yet subtle enough for everyone, has been established regarding His complete power to distinguish their dust from the dust of the earth, to distinguish some of their dust from other dust, and to distinguish the dust of each part of them, whether large or small, from the rest, it becomes known that the implied meaning is: ﴿then He will return you to a new creation, as you were the first time﴾. He omitted it, as is (p-٢٤٩) the Qur'an's habit of omitting whatever the context indicates when there is no reason to mention it. He then joined to it His words: ﴿Then to your Lord you will be returned﴾, that is, to the One who originated your creation and your nurture and who bestowed upon you the utmost of kindness from the beginning, and not to anyone else, after your restoration, ﴿you will be returned﴾, by Him raising you up as a single soul, whereupon you will be before Him. Thus His kindness and His lordship are fulfilled by recompensing each one for what he did, as is the custom of kings with their servants, none of whom leaves a wrongdoing servant unpunished.

When the proof of the Resurrection had been established by what admits no doubt or ambiguity, he began to relate some of their conditions at that time, saying, turning away from addressing them in contempt for them and as a declaration of wrath, and addressing the Prophet ﷺ as consolation to him, or to everyone whose address is valid, coordinating it with what its implied sense is: "Then if you could see them when the graves have been overturned, and what is in the breasts has been brought out, and there are matters there, what matters!" He placed the present tense in a position where it is proper for the past tense to enter, because it is certain to occur, as if it had already occurred. The expression with it was chosen to refresh the soul by anticipating seeing it at the moment of hearing it, hastening joy through anticipating the calamity for the people of evil: ﴿And if you could see﴾, meaning, you, the one who sees, would be among those who see, in order to see the state of ﴿the criminals﴾, meaning those who severed what God commanded to be joined, ﴿when they have bowed their heads before their Lord﴾, meaning they lower them in shame, fear, disgrace and humiliation at the place of reckoning, ﴿before their Lord﴾, the One who does good to them and who alone manages their affairs, saying in utmost humiliation and tenderness: ﴿Our Lord﴾, meaning, O You who do good to us, ﴿we have seen﴾ what we used to deny, ﴿and we have heard﴾, meaning from You and from Your angels and from the voices of the fires and other things, what we used to consider far-fetched, so we have come to the utmost knowledge of the completeness of Your power and the truthfulness of Your promises, ﴿so send us back﴾ with what You possess of this attribute which requires goodness, to the abode of deeds, ﴿that we may do righteousness﴾. Then they confirmed this promise by saying, by way of giving a reason, emphasizing it, because their state was that of one in doubt whom the addressee would hesitate to convince: ﴿Indeed, we are certain﴾, meaning: there is now established for us certainty concerning everything we were informed of from You that has been disclosed by direct vision. That is, if you saw that, you would see a matter which the intellect cannot bear because of its terror and magnitude, and which no description can encompass.

ولَمّا لَمْ يَذْكُرْ لَهم جَوابًا، عُلِمَ أنَّهُ لِهَوانِهِمْ، لِأنَّهُ ما جَرَّأهم عَلى (p-٢٥١)العِصْيانِ إلّا صِفَةُ الإحْسانِ، فَلا يَصْلُحُ لَهم إلّا الخِزْيُ والهَوانُ، ولِأنَّ الإيمانَ لا يَصِحُّ إلّا بِالغَيْبِ (al-ghayb: the unseen) قَبْلَ العِيانِ (al-'iyan: direct witnessing).

When he did not mention an answer for them, it was understood that this was because of their abasement, since nothing emboldened them to disobedience except the attribute of kindness, so nothing suits them except disgrace and humiliation. And because faith is not valid except through the unseen before direct witnessing.

ولَمّا كانَ رُبَّما وقَعَ في وهْمِ أنَّ ضَلالَهم مَعَ الإمْعانِ في البَيانِ، لِعَجَزَ عَنْ هِدايَتِهِمْ أوْ تَوانٍ، قالَ عاطِفًا [عَلى] ما تَقْدِيرُهُ: إنِّي لا أرُدُّكم لِأنِّي لَمْ أُضِلَّكم في الدُّنْيا لِلْعَجْزِ عَنْ هِدايَتِكم فِيها، بَلْ لِأنِّي لَمْ أُرِدْ إسْعادَكُمْ، ولَوْ شِئْتُ لَهَدَيْتُكُمْ، [صارِفًا القَوْلَ إلى مَظْهَرِ العَظَمَةِ لِاقْتِضاءِ المَقامِ لَها:] ﴿ولَوْ شِئْنا﴾ أيْ: بِما لَنا مِنَ العَظَمَةِ الَّتِي تَأْبى أنْ يَكُونَ لِغَيْرِنا شَيْءٌ يَسْتَقِلُّ بِهِ أوْ يَكُونُ في مِلْكِنا ما لا نُرِيدُ ﴿لآتَيْنا كُلَّ نَفْسٍ﴾ أيْ: مُكَلَّفَةٍ لِأنَّ الكَلامَ فِيها ﴿هُداها﴾ أيْ: جَعَلْنا هِدايَتَها ورُشْدَها وتَوْفِيقَها لِلْإيمانِ وجَمِيعِ ما يَتْبَعُهُ مِن صالِحِ الأعْمالِ في يَدِها مُتَمَكِّنَةً مِنها.

Because the matter might occur to the mind that their going astray, despite the thorough clarification, was due to His inability to guide them or to His negligence, He said, linking [to] what is implied: "I do not reject you because I did not cause you to go astray in this world through inability to guide you in it; rather, it is because I did not will your happiness. Had I willed, I would have guided you," [turning the speech toward the manifestation of greatness, as the situation requires it:] ﴿And had We willed﴾, that is, by what We possess of greatness, which refuses that anything other than Us should have something it can independently control, or that there should be in Our dominion what We do not want, ﴿We would have given every soul﴾, that is, every accountable soul, since the discussion concerns it, ﴿its guidance﴾, that is, We would have made its guidance, its right direction, and its success in faith and in all the righteous deeds that follow from it, within its power, with it being able to exercise them.

ولَمّا اسْتَوْفى الأمْرُ حَدَّهُ مِنَ العَظَمَةِ، لَفَتَ الكَلامَ إلى الإفْرادِ، دَفْعًا لِلتَّعَنُّتِ وتَحْقِيقًا لِأنَّ المُرادَ بِالأوَّلِ العَظَمَةُ فَقالَ: ﴿ولَكِنْ﴾ أيْ: لَمْ أشَأْ ذَلِكَ لِأنَّهُ ﴿حَقَّ القَوْلُ مِنِّي﴾ وأنا مَن لا يُخْلِفُ المِيعادَ، لِأنَّ الإخْلافَ إمّا لِعَجْزٍ أوْ نِسْيانٍ أوْ حاجَةٍ ولا شَيْءَ مِن ذَلِكَ يَلِيقُ بِجَنابِي، أوْ يَحِلُّ بِساحَتِي، وأكَّدَ لِأجْلِ إنْكارِهِمْ فَقالَ مُقْسِمًا: ﴿لأمْلأنَّ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ (p-٢٥٢)الَّتِي هي مَحَلُّ إهانَتِي وتَجَهُّمِ أعْدائِي بِما تَجَهَّمُوا أوْلِيائِي ﴿مِنَ الجِنَّةِ﴾ أيِ: الجِنِّ طائِفَةِ إبْلِيسَ، وكَأنَّهُ أنَّثَهم تَحْقِيرًا لَهم عِنْدَ مَن يَسْتَعْظِمُ أمْرَهم لِما دَعا إلى تَحْقِيرِهِمْ مِن مَقامِ الغَضَبِ وبَدَأ بِهِمْ لِاسْتِعْظامِهِمْ لَهم ولِأنَّهُمُ الَّذِينَ أضَلُّوهم ﴿والنّاسِ أجْمَعِينَ﴾ حَيْثُ قُلْتُ لِإبْلِيسَ: ﴿لأمْلأنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنكَ ومِمَّنْ تَبِعَكَ مِنهم أجْمَعِينَ﴾ [ص: ٨٥] فَلِذَلِكَ شِئْتُ كُفْرَ الكافِرِ وعِصْيانَ العاصِي بَعْدَ أنْ جَعَلْتُ لَهُمُ اخْتِيارًا، وغَيَّبْتُ العاقِبَةَ عَنْهُمْ، فَصارَ الكَسْبُ يُنْسَبُ إلَيْهِمْ ظاهِرًا، والخَلْقُ في الحَقِيقَةِ والمَشِيئَةُ لِي.

When the matter had reached the full limit of greatness, he turned the speech to the singular, to repel obstinacy and to affirm that what is meant by the first [form] is greatness, and so He said: ﴿But [it is] that﴾, that is, I did not will that, because ﴿the word has come into effect from Me﴾, and I am the One who does not break the promise, since breaking it is either from inability, forgetfulness, or need, and none of these befits My presence or descends upon My court. And He emphasized it, for the sake of their denial, and so He said, swearing an oath: ﴿"I will surely fill Hell"﴾ (p-٢٥٢), which is the place of My humiliation and the frowning upon My enemies, for they frowned upon My friends, ﴿with the jinn﴾, that is, the jinn, the group of Iblis. It is as if He used the feminine form to belittle them in the eyes of one who magnifies their affair, since the situation of wrath called for belittling them, and He began with them, to emphasize them, and because they are the ones who led them astray, ﴿and mankind, all together﴾, where I said to Iblis: ﴿"I will surely fill Hell with you and with whoever follows you of them, all together"﴾ [Sad: 85]. Therefore I willed the disbelief of the disbeliever and the disobedience of the disobedient after I granted them choice and concealed the consequence from them, so that the acquisition is ascribed to them outwardly, while the creation in reality and the will belong to Me.

When the truth of this statement made it certain that there was no escape from their punishment, He said, responding to their softening at that time and negating what their speech might imply, namely that He is in need of worship: ﴿So taste﴾, meaning: [taste] what you used to deny, because of what was decreed from Me, ﴿because you forgot the meeting of this your day﴾, meaning: because of [the fact that] ﴿you forgot the meeting of this your day﴾ [He emphasized it], and He clarified for them by His saying ﴿this﴾, meaning: you did, in turning away from preparing for this standing-place, in which you will be called to account and in which justice will be manifest, the deed of one who forgets it. This is despite the fact that it is ingrained in your natures that it is not fitting for one possessed of knowledge and wisdom to leave His servants frolicking on His earth and moving about in His provision, and then not call them to account for that and not give justice to the wronged among them. So turning away from Him deserved to be called forgetting from this aspect too, and from the aspect that, since the proofs that filled the cosmos had become manifest to you, your turning away became as if it had not appeared, and it is related: "then he forgot." Then He gave the reason for their tasting of that, or began [a new statement] to explain the recompense for it, emphasizing it in the mode of greatness, to cut off their hopes of deliverance. For this reason He returned to the mode of greatness and said: ﴿Indeed We have forgotten you﴾, meaning: We have dealt with you by what belongs to Us of greatness and what belongs to you of lowliness, treating you as one who forgets treats [those he has forgotten]. So We brought you to the Fire, just as We swore that none of you would fail to pass through it, then We brought out the people of Our love and left you in it, [leaving you] as the forgotten are left.

Since the previous command to taste was general, He clarified it with His saying, emphasizing it: ﴿And taste the punishment of eternity﴾, meaning: the one specifically characterized as having no end. Since He had specified the cause earlier, He here generalized it, saying: ﴿because of what you used to do﴾, meaning: by natural disposition and inclination ﴿working﴾ from the deeds of one who did not fear the matter of resurrection, intending that you would never desist from that.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 32, verse 15:

Since His saying, ﴿Nay, but they are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord﴾ [al-Sajdah: 10], had indicated that what drives them to disbelief is arrogance (al-kibar), and since He, glorified be He, mentioned that He divided people into two groups for the sake of the two abodes, the soul yearned to hear the mark of the people of faith, just as the mark of the people of disbelief had been mentioned. So He said, making known that the criminals have no path to their faith: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-An'am: 28]. ﴿Those only believe in Our verses﴾, which indicate Our greatness, ﴿who, when they are reminded of them﴾, by whatever reminder it is, at whatever time it is, before the lifting of the veil and after it, ﴿fall down in prostration﴾, meaning they hasten to prostrate with the haste of one who falls without intending to, humbling themselves before Allah out of the intensity of their humility, their fear, and their submissiveness to Him, a submission that is firm and constant. ﴿And they glorify﴾, meaning they exercise tanzih (declaring Allah free of every flaw of deficiency), including abstaining from frivolity that leads to the squandering of wisdom and other things, ﴿with the praise of﴾, and He turned the speech to the attribute that necessitates their tanzih and their praise, as an alert to them, so He said: ﴿their Lord﴾, meaning by their affirming for Him the encompassing of the attributes of perfection. Since this included their humility, He stated it explicitly in His saying: ﴿and they are not arrogant﴾, meaning they do not renew the seeking of arrogance regarding anything to which the Guide has called them, nor do they make it a settled trait lodged in their hearts.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 32, verse 16:

Since the humble person is sometimes accused of laziness, he negated that of them by saying, clarifying with what the preceding verse included of their fear: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds﴾, meaning they rise up with the rising of one who goes to the utmost in forsaking, which is indicated by the use of the apparent noun (al-izhar), and he gave good news of their great number by using the plural of abundance (jam' al-kathrah), so he said: ﴿their sides﴾ after sleep ﴿from their couches﴾, meaning the well-spread, prepared beds which are [the place of] rest, tranquility and sleep. They are thus as though stung by scorpions upon them, unable to settle upon them during the night, which is the place of seclusion and the site of the pleasure and joy of what the souls desire. [Imam al-Suhrawardi said in the forty-sixth chapter of his 'Awarif (ʿAwārif al-Maʿārif) concerning the lovers: It was said: their sleep is the sleep of the sick, their eating is the eating of the ill, and their speech is a necessity. Whoever sleeps out of being overpowered, with a gathered concern attached to standing in the night, is granted success in standing in the night. The soul, when it is fed and accustomed to sleep, indulges in it; but when it is stirred by the sincerity of resolve, it does not indulge in settling. This stirring of the soul by sincerity of resolve is the forsaking (tajafi) which God mentioned, because the concern for standing in the night and sincerity of resolve make the side and the bed equal, and make for forsaking.]

Since forsaking the bed may occur for other than worship, he made clear that it is for worship, so he said, clarifying their state: ﴿they call upon﴾, meaning on a continuous basis, and he made apparent the attribute which emboldened them to ask, so he said: ﴿their Lord﴾, meaning the One who accustomed them with His goodness. Then he gave the reason for their supplication by his saying: ﴿in fear﴾, meaning of His wrath and punishment. [For the causes of fear arising from their shortcomings are many, whether or not they know a particular cause that necessitates fear; thus they do not feel safe from His scheme, since He may do whatever He wills.] ﴿and in hope﴾, meaning for His good pleasure which necessitates His reward. He expressed it with (tama') rather than (raja'), indicating that because of their intense knowledge of their shortcomings, they do not consider their deeds to be anything, but rather they seek His bounty without cause. [And if they hope for His mercy without cause, they are even more hopeful with cause; thus they do not despair of His comfort.]

Since worship cuts one off from expanding in this world, the soul of the worshipper may at times incline to clinging to what is in his hand, out of fear that worship falls short of need due to the confusion of thought and the movement to seek sustenance, he urged spending from it, relying upon the Creator, the Provider, who guaranteed the replacement, so that they would be more trusting in what He guaranteed for them than in what is in their own hands, and as an announcement that prayer is a cause of blessing in provision: ﴿And enjoin your family to prayer and be steadfast in it; We do not ask you for provision, We provide for you﴾ [Ta-Ha: 132]. So he said, turning attention to the manifestation of greatness, as an admonition that provision is from Him alone: ﴿And from what We have provided them﴾, meaning by Our greatness, with no power or strength from them, ﴿they spend﴾, without extravagance or stinginess, in all the ways of nearness to God which We have legislated for them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 32, verse 17:

When He had mentioned the recompense of the arrogant, the soul yearned to know the recompense of the humble, so He pointed to their recompense with the fa' of causation (fa' al-sabab), indicating that it is He who, by His mercy, enabled them to do these deeds and made them a means to entering His Paradise. Had He willed, it would have been otherwise. [So He said:] ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them﴾, meaning, of all souls, neither a near angel nor anyone else, ﴿of what is hidden for them﴾, meaning for these who remember, from the One who knows the keys of the unseen and its treasuries, just as they used to conceal their deeds of prayer in the depth of the night and other such things, and did not show them off. Perhaps it was built in the passive form (ukhfiya) in the reading of the majority (al-jama'ah) to magnify it, since the mind goes off into the hidden in every direction, or because of the knowledge that it is Allah Most High for whose sake they concealed the voluntary acts of their deeds. Hamzah read the yā' with sukūn, taking it as the first person of the Speaker, glory be to Him, shifting from the style of majesty to the style of gentleness; the secret of this is its suitability to the state of the deeds.

Since the eye does not become cool and drift into sleep except in security and joy, He said: ﴿of comfort for the eyes﴾, meaning of something precious and delightful by which their eyes are made cool, because they removed their eyes from their resting place by sleep. Then He stated explicitly what the fa' of causation had conveyed, so He said: ﴿as a recompense﴾, meaning He concealed it for them as a recompense ﴿for what they used to﴾ [do], meaning for what was theirs as a disposition (kal-jibillah) ﴿they used to do﴾. Al-Bukhari narrated in the Tafsir from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived." Abu Hurayrah said: Recite, if you wish: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them﴾, to the end of the verse.

(p-258) Since they were people of eloquence, fluency and skill, and of disputation, it would often happen that their contentious opponent would say: "What is the matter with Him, if what you claim is true, that He does not care about anything and nothing diminishes from His treasuries, and He is the Mighty, the Merciful, who does not make equal all of them in entering Paradise and in bestowing bounty with blessings, so that He would encompass them with the manifest mercy just as He encompassed them with it in this world, as is the custom of the good-doers?" As a consequence of that, He said, denouncing it and indicating that what prevents it is that it would go beyond wisdom, since that abode is the abode of recompense and this is the abode of action, and between them there is a great distinction: ﴿Is then one who was⦆ i.e., in a state that, owing to its firmness, is like a natural disposition, ﴿a believer⦆ i.e., firmly established in the great affirmation of everything the Messengers reported, ﴿like one who was⦆ [Since the context was arranged upon the proof of ﴿You have no protector or intercessor besides Him⦆ [al-Sajdah: 4], and the verse, so the disbeliever was outside the encompassing of that proof, which is not hidden in any way from anyone who has hearing, sight and heart, the situation required the expression of corruption (fisq), which is going outside the encompassing, so He said:] ﴿a deviator⦆ i.e., firmly established in deviation, outside the circle of submission.

Since the interrogation was directed at everyone who was characterized by this description, and the interrogation was denunciatory, He expressed its meaning explicitly by His saying: ﴿They are not equal⦆. This is an indication, through treating the word "one who" (man) once according to its form and once according to its meaning, that a group of these people is not equal to a group of those, nor an individual to an individual.

(p-259) When He negated their equality, He followed it with the state of each group in detail, expressing it in the plural. This is because judging His being pleased or displeased with a person by understanding the wisdoms behind it applies to an individual among them *a fortiori*. So He said: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾, meaning: confirming their faith ﴿with righteous deeds, for them are the gardens of refuge (jannat al-ma'wa)﴾, meaning the gardens specific to the hereafter, not the worldly ones, which are a place of passing through, and not the Fire, which is a place of flight rather than of settling. This is because they are fit for the perfect abode in this description, as indicated by the definite article in "al-" (ال), abiding therein and not seeking any change from it, just as they had settled into faith, which is fit for dwelling, so they did not seek any substitute for it. ﴿As a welcome gift (nuzul)﴾, meaning provisions prepared for them at the first moment of their arrival, according to the view of al-Hasan and 'Ata', and this is more fitting to the context, just as provision is prepared for a guest, as is apparent. ﴿For what they used to do﴾, by disposition and by nature, ﴿doing﴾ constantly, in a renewing manner, for their deeds are themselves from the mercy of their Lord. If these gardens are a welcome gift, then what do you think of what lies beyond that! By my life, this is what the Prophet (ﷺ) indicated when he said: "Something no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and it has not occurred to the heart of any human being." And they are, every moment, in increase, because the power of Allah has no end. So beware lest a deceiver deceive you, or a heretic delude you.

(p-260) **"And as for those who defied (fasaqū)"**, that is, who went outside the sphere of faith, which is the source of humility and is worthy of companionship and constant association, **"their abode is the Fire"**, that is, a Fire that has no fitness whatsoever for sheltering them in any way at all.

Since the listener was deserving of knowing that they strive to escape from it, He said, beginning a new sentence (*mustaʾnifan*) to explain their condition: **"Every time they wish [i.e. while they are gathered together, so how much more when some of them wish] to come out of it"**. This indicates that their punishment is increased by their being made to imagine that they have the ability to get out of it, just as they used to go out, through their defiance, from the encompassing of the proofs [and] from the sphere of acts of obedience into the wastelands of disobedience and lapses. So they attempt to get out, and when they think it has become easy for them, while they are still in its depths, **"they will be returned"** with the easiest and most effortless command from whoever gives that order, **"into it"**, to the place where they were at first. This will remain their constant condition forever. **"And it will be said"**, that is, by whatever speaker has been appointed over them, **"to them"**, that is, at the time of their being returned, as a humiliation to them: **"Taste the punishment of the Fire"**.

Since He had described their punishment in the Fire, it was more fitting to use the description when explaining the cause of the humiliation, by the command to "taste". Yet it was also more fitting, in terms of its being an addition (*muḍāf*) about which information is given (*muḥaddath ʿanhu*), so He said: **"which you used to"**, that is, a state that belongs to you as an inherent nature, **"[so] by it you deny"**. He indicates that their denial of it (the Fire) causes every other denial to vanish in its presence, so it seems to be specific to it. Then He said: **"by it you deny"**, for the return after the attempt to exit is more conducive to belief, in view of the renewal at every moment.

(p-261) Since the believers were now wishing that some measure of humiliation in this world would befall them, because human souls are created with a disposition toward hastiness, He gave them good news of this in a way that includes the punishment of the grave. He said, emphasizing it [for them], because of their denial of the punishment after death and of affliction in this world, given the multitude and strength they possessed: ﴿And We will surely make them taste﴾, that is, all of them, directly and through causes, by means of the greatness We possess, before which their multitude and strength vanish, ﴿of the lesser punishment﴾, that is, before the Day of Resurrection, at your hands and by other means. Allah has indeed fulfilled His word. When this surah was revealed in Makkah, the Honored, they were at the height of abundance and blessing, and He made them taste famine for consecutive years, scattered their unity, and killed and captured them at the hands of the believers, and other things as He willed, may He be glorified. Then He affirmed the intent regarding what precedes the Hereafter and confirmed it by His saying, expressing it with a term suited to a lesser and inferior degree: ﴿short of the greater punishment﴾, that is, the one previously mentioned, in the Hereafter, ﴿that perhaps they will return﴾, that is, so that their state would be that of one whose return from his corruption is hoped for by the one who gives him respite. This did occur: many of them returned out of fear of the sword, and when they saw the excellences of Islam, they became among the most eager of people for it and the most loving of it.

(p-262) Since the implied sense is: "they should return from their wrongdoing, for they are wrongdoers," he linked to it [His saying:] "And who is more unjust" than them? This is the original structure, but He made apparent the attribute by which they became more unjust, and so said: "than one who is reminded" — that is, by whatever reminder it may be — and He turned the speech toward the attribute of benevolence, as a means of winning them over and alerting them to the obligation of gratitude, so He said: "of the signs of his Lord" — that is, the One from whom there is no blessing except from Him.

When these verses reached the utmost clarity, such that turning away from them became far-fetched after that, He expressed it with the particle of distance for this reason, and said: "then turns away from them," the opposite of what those did who could not restrain themselves from falling down in prostration. It is also permissible — and it is the better reading — that "then" (thumma) be in its proper sense of delay, so that the meaning is that whoever is reminded of them at some time, then begins to reflect upon them, then turns away from them after that, even after a thousand years, he is the most unjust of the wrongdoers. What is less than this is included by way of a fortiori reasoning, because it is more likely to avoid forgetting. Thus it is more eloquent than the expression with "fa" (then, immediately), as in Surat al-Kahf. He had shifted to "fa" there to explain what their condition would be when they asked for a clarification, whose clarification they made the sign of truthfulness and the inability to produce a sign of falsehood.

Since the situation called for a question about their recompense, and He had made the pronoun singular in view of the word "man" (who), to alert to the ugliness of wrongdoing from every individual (p-263), He said, gathering them together — because the humiliation of the plural indicates the humiliation of the singular a fortiori — emphasizing it — because their boldness in denying is like rejecting the one who was reminded, as they transgressed against him — turning the direction of the speech away from the attribute of benevolence, as a notice of anger: "Indeed We" — from among them; this is what the original structure was. But He made apparent the attribute explicitly, for generality, and to attach the judgment to it, specifying the type of their wrongdoing to make it abhorrent, so He said: "from the criminals" — that is, those who sever what ought to be joined, specifically — "[are] avengers." He expressed it with the form of greatness, to alert that what befalls them of punishment does not fall under the mere description of being counted among the wrongdoers; how much more so, since they were the most unjust of the wrongdoers? The nominal sentence indicates the continuance of this upon them: in this world, either inwardly through being led on gradually by blessings, or outwardly through the descent of vengeance; and in the Hereafter, through the perpetuity of punishment over the passing of ages.

Since the central theme of the surah is the negation of doubt concerning the revelation of this Clear Book, that it is from the Lord of the worlds, and it indicates that turning away from it is only wrongdoing and obstinacy, He concluded it with a threat against turning away from the signs with retribution. [He] (Allah, glorified is He) had already taken vengeance on those who made light of Moses (peace be upon him), both before the Book was sent down to him and after it was sent down. He was the first to whom a book was revealed among the Children of Israel, after a long interval of prophets between him and Joseph (peace be upon them both). They all believed in him, Allah united them through him, and He rescued them from the captivity of the Qibt (the Copts) at his hand. He mentioned this as a matter of consolation and encouragement for those who accepted, a threat for those who turned away, and good news of the faith of all the Arabs, their unification through it, and the deliverance of the people of Yemen from the captivity of the Persians by means of it. So He said, emphasizing it as an alert for whoever thinks that the Mighty cannot be opposed in any of His affairs: ﴿And We had certainly given﴾, by the greatness that belongs to Us, ﴿Moses the Book﴾ [i.e., the one comprising the rulings], which is the Tawrat (the Torah).

Since that is likewise something without doubt, and since his people had abandoned following much of it, especially what it related of the attributes of our Prophet (ﷺ) and what it commanded regarding following him, and since this was a turning away on their part like the turning away of one who doubts something, and since in the time of Moses (peace be upon him) too they used to oppose his commands time after time and moment after moment, the statement ﴿So do not be﴾ followed the mention of the giving, alluding to them and informing that the Mighty may wish to [reject] some of His commands for a wisdom He has arranged. ﴿Do not be﴾ means a firm state, indicated by the verb of being and the retention of its nun, so it conveys the pardon of the inner thoughts that arise in the community, as he (ﷺ) explained. ﴿In doubt﴾, i.e., suspicion, ﴿about meeting him﴾, i.e., do not act in that matter as one who doubts the meeting with Moses (peace be upon him) [regarding the Book] from Us, and receiving it with contentment, acceptance and submission, as those did who claimed to follow him and act by his Book, while turning away from the religion of Islam to which he called them. Or: do not act as one who doubts your meeting with the Book from Us, even if they attribute to you fabrication, and even if some of what it reports is delayed; it will be guidance for whoever remains of them and a punishment for those who have passed, and no report of what it announced as future will remain without coming to pass exactly as it was announced, for you receive it from One who is All-Wise, All-Knowing. Moses (peace be upon him) also endured in receiving his Book and in his call until he died in the best of states. Or the meaning is: We had certainly given Moses the Book, and there was disagreement about it [concerning him], yet none of the steadfast doubted Our giving him the Book because of the turning away of those who turned away, nor was the faltering of those who turned their backs a cause; We took vengeance on those who turned away from it. So let none of those who believed in you be in doubt about Our giving you the Book, because of the turning away of those whom I turn away; We will destroy those whom We have decreed to be wretched, as vengeance upon them, and make happy those who remain through it.

When He indicated their turning away from it and the turning away of the Arabs from their Book, He mentioned that all of them had, by that misguidance, done the opposite of what the Book was sent down for. So He said, bestowing favor upon (p-266) the Children of Israel and giving good news to the Arabs: ﴿And We made it﴾, i.e., the Book of Moses (peace be upon him), in a manner befitting Our greatness, ﴿a guidance﴾, i.e., a great clarification, ﴿for the Children of Israel﴾

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 32, verse 24:

He pointed to their disagreement about it by His saying: ﴿And We made from among them﴾, i.e., from among their prophets and rabbis, by Our greatness, despite what is in human nature of following desire, ﴿leaders guiding﴾, i.e., they convey the clear exposition and act in accordance with it, ﴿by Our command﴾, i.e., by what We sent down in it of commands.
