Then he mentioned the reason for Our making that for them by His saying: ﴿when they were patient﴾, i.e., because of their patience and for its sake, according to the reading of Hamzah and al-Kisa'i with kasra and takhfif (lightening of the consonant), or when He made them patient in accepting Our commands, according to the reading of the rest with fatha and tashdid (doubling of the consonant), though patience is also only by Allah's granting of success to them. ﴿And they were certain of Our signs﴾, because of their greatness, ﴿they did not doubt any of them, nor did they act as one who doubts about them by turning away; and that was [for them] a disposition We had created in them.

When he said "from among them," it made clear that among them were those who strayed from the command of God and turned others away from it. Then His words came as consolation to the believers and a warning to the disbelievers. It is an emphatic resumptive clause (istiʾnaf), serving to alert anyone who thinks there will be no resurrection, and the speech turns to the attribute of ihsan (beneficence) to indicate what appears of the Prophet's (ﷺ) nobility on that day [in that Day], including the praised station (al-maqam al-mahmud) and other things: ﴿Indeed your Lord﴾, that is, the One who has been beneficent to you by sending you, so that He magnifies your reward and elevates your station (p-267) ﴿Himself﴾, that is, alone, ﴿will judge between them﴾, that is, between the guided and the misguided and the astray, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾, with the true judgment, so He elevates the cause of the oppressed and brings to nothing the scheme of the oppressor, ﴿concerning that about which they used to differ﴾, that is, by nature and disposition, ﴿concerning it﴾, that is, specifically, ﴿they used to differ﴾, that is, they continually renewed their disagreement about it in a persistent manner according to what they were disposed to, and nothing of it is hidden from Him. As for what they differed about other than this, the ruling concerning it is in their favor or against them, not between them. And what they differed about without intent falls within the realm of pardon.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 32, verse 26:

Since two statements of the disbelievers have preceded in this surah, the first concerning the denial of the Qur'an and the second concerning the denial of resurrection, and since He, glory be to Him, refuted both of them until He concluded with the mention of the signs, the resurrection, and the distinction between the truthful and the falsifier, He followed this with two rhetorical questions of denial, applied to both statements [and the verse of each of them was concluded with another, so the interrogatives become four]. In the object of the first is the distinction between the two groups in this world. So He said, threatening: ﴿Has it not⁠﻿ become clear﴾, that is, do they say, out of obstinacy toward Our Messenger: "Has he invented it?" And it has not ﴿become clear﴾, that is, it has not been made manifest, as al-Bukhari transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, ﴿to them how many We destroyed﴾, that is, the multitude of those whom We destroyed.

Since nearness of a thing in time or place is more indicative, He specified their nearness by introducing the preposition, and so He said: ﴿before them﴾, that is, on account of their opposition to the messengers, ﴿of the generations﴾ who passed away, of those who turned away from the signs, while We saved those who believed in them. [Perhaps] nearness of place is a station close to nearness of time, owing to the frequency of reminder through the remains and the passing through the abodes.

Since their absorption in the fleeting world had preoccupied them from reflecting on what benefits them from admonitions by deeds and words, He indicated this by depicting their awareness of their own circumstances, through His saying: ﴿they walk⁠﻿﴾, that is, they are not people capable of reflection except while walking ﴿in their dwellings﴾, owing to the intensity of their attachment to sensible things. This is like the dwellings of 'Ad, Thamud, the people of Lot, and others like them. Since in this there is the most complete lesson and the greatest admonition, He said, alerting to it and emphasizing it, as an alert that whoever does not take heed denies what is in it of lessons: ﴿Indeed in that⁠﻿﴾, that is, in this great matter, ﴿are signs﴾, that is, very clear indications, seen in the dwellings and other remains, and heard in reports.

Since hearing is the greatest pillar, and since the destruction of the generations reached them only through hearing, He said, denouncing: ﴿Do they not then hear?﴾, that is, the circumstances of those mentioned to them do not require, for one who is reminded of them to turn back from error, any other than hearing them. [If he does not turn back, then he is among those who have no hearing.]

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 32, verse 27:

﴿Do they not see﴾, i.e., do they say, in denying the resurrection: "When we have gone astray in the earth..."? And they have not seen ﴿that We drive the water﴾, by what We possess of greatness, ﴿to the barren land﴾, from the sky or from the earth, ﴿to the barren land﴾, i.e., the land whose vegetation has withered (jaraza nabatuha), meaning it has been cut off by dryness and crumbling, i.e., by human hands, so it became smooth, with no plant in it. In al-Bukhari, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: it is the land that receives only a rain that does not benefit it in any way. They said: "What does not grow, like salt flats, is not called juruz." This is supported by His saying: ﴿so We bring forth thereby﴾ from the depths of the earth ﴿crops﴾, i.e., plants without stalks, through the mixing of water with the soil that had been cultivated before this. He indicated that this is a real matter, with no doubt about it, and it is not an illusion as the sorcerers do, by His saying, reminding them of the blessing of sustenance after bringing into existence: ﴿of which eat their livestock﴾, i.e., of its grain, its leaves, its straw and its herbage. He placed the livestock first because of the context of granting favor through them, since by them their subsistence and bodies are sustained, and because the context concerns the bringing forth of crops in general, whose first benefit is for the eating of livestock. This differs from what is in Surat 'Abasa, where the context concerns human food, which is the end of the crop, when He said: ﴿Let man look at his food﴾ [Abasa: 24], then said ﴿and We split the earth in it, splitting it open, and caused grain to grow in it﴾ [Abasa: 27], and He mentioned among his food grapes and other things that are not suitable for livestock. ﴿and themselves﴾, i.e., from its grain, and its origin is when it is green herbage.

And since this verse is [a clear sign, and was] in its clarity as proof of the resurrection, such that the one ignorant of it needs nothing for acknowledgment except seeing it, He said: ﴿Will they not then see?﴾, indicating that whoever has seen it, become alert to the proof within it, and yet persists in denial, has neither sight nor insight.

When this verse was the most conclusive proof—as has passed—of the resurrection, and that day is one in which the might of the allies of God is manifested and the humiliation of the enemies, He followed it with His saying, in wonder at them, coordinated with "They say, 'He has forged it'" and its like: ﴿And they say﴾, that is, despite this clear explanation which admits no confusion, mockingly: ﴿"When is this victory?"﴾, that is, the aid, the judgment and the decision that opens what is closed on the Day of Gathering ﴿"if you are ﴾, that is, in a firm state ﴿truthful"﴾, that is, deeply rooted in truthfulness in reporting that it must certainly occur, so that we may believe when we see it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 32, verse 29:

When their condition became clear through this question, whose underlying purpose is urgency, asked in a mocking manner, showing that they only increase in obstinacy when the clarification is given, He commanded them with a reply containing the most forceful threat. So He said, acting as one who is able and who turns away from answering them about specifying the day, up to mentioning its condition: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to these stubborn ignoramuses: ﴿On the Day of Victory﴾, that is, the day at which they mock, which is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿their faith will not benefit those who disbelieved﴾, that is, those who covered over the signs of their Lord which are beyond any concealment, whether this applies to you or to others who share this attribute. ﴿Their faith﴾ [will not benefit them], because it is not faith in the unseen, but He drove it in this manner as one drives what is known. ﴿Nor will they be reprieved﴾, that is, they will not be granted respite, at the moment the punishment befalls them, for even a single instant.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 32, verse 30:

When the outcome of their hearing these proofs was their mockery, to the extent that they even asked about the Day of Victory (al-Fath), and He, glorified is He, answered them regarding its specification by mentioning its circumstances, and the Prophet (ﷺ), out of his intense eagerness for their benefit, sometimes loved to inform them of what they asked for, even though he knew that this (asking) was from them as mockery, hoping that it would benefit them in some measure, Allah, glorified is He, made consequent upon his turning away from answering them his command to this gentle caller and compassionate guide to likewise turn away from them. So He said, consoling him and threatening them: ﴿So turn away from them﴾ [i.e.,] paying no heed to them, even if their harm intensifies, ﴿and wait﴾, i.e., (wait to see) what We will do to them of that which manifests your affair and raises your religion. And since the situation required that the listener might doubt about their state, whether it was (really) waiting, He answered by way of emphasis with His words: ﴿Indeed they are waiting﴾, i.e., (waiting to see) what will be done to you and what the outcome of your affair will be, regarding what you threaten them with and other than that. The end of this (surah) has corresponded to its beginning through the warning with this Book, and He made known, by its majesty, its eloquence, its severity and its courage, that there is no kind of doubt in it. Also, its beginning concerns denial of its revelation, and its end concerns mockery of its fulfilment (ta'wil),

﴿On the Day its fulfilment comes, those who had forgotten it before will say...﴾ [al-A'raf: 53] — the verse. Also, the beginning concerns denial of the sending down of the spiritual spirit (al-ruh al-ma'nawi), and the end concerns denial of the restoration of the physical, sensory spirit which He originated the first time. And Allah is the Guide to what is right.
